source: Select-then-Solve (2026) Paradigm Routing as Inference-Time Optimization for LLM Agents: oracle gap
finding: Per-item oracle choice among 5 reasoning paradigms beats the best fixed paradigm by a wide margin on every model. Answers gap 2: headroom is large on a mixed suite.
numbers: 4 models, 10 benchmarks, 761 tasks per model-paradigm pair. Table 3 oracle vs best single: GPT-5 74.1 vs 61.8 (+12.4); Gemini-Flash 75.2 vs 56.1 (+19.1); Qwen3-Max 72.5 vs 46.5 (+21.6); Qwen3-30B 55.7 vs 31.7 (+24.1). Paper states +17.1 average; its own tables give 19.3 to 20.4, so it is internally inconsistent.
quote: No single paradigm dominates, and oracle per-task selection beats the best fixed paradigm by 17.1pp on average.
limits: Oracle takes the max over noisy single runs, so it is optimistic. Gap spans 10 very different benchmarks, not one class.
agent_relevance: A class record only pays if classes differ in best operator. Here they do. Measure our own oracle gap with repeats to remove noise.

source: Select-then-Solve (2026): learned router vs best fixed paradigm
finding: A supervised router on prompt features beats the best fixed paradigm modestly and recovers only a quarter to a third of the oracle gap. Closest test of gap 1.
numbers: Table 7 held-out accuracy, mean of 4 models: Direct 47.6, best single 50.3, Combined-LR router 53.1, oracle 68.9. Gap recovery about 26 percent mean (31 GPT-5, 37 Gemini). Router vs best single: GPT-5 64.2 vs 62.4; Gemini 61.0 vs 55.5; Qwen3-Max 54.6 vs 50.7; Qwen3-30B 32.8 vs 32.8 (no gain).
limits: Test set 229 tasks, one seed, no CIs; 2 to 3 point gains are within noise for some models. Router learns task type from embeddings, not from a written record. No random-router control.
agent_relevance: Expect a few points from a class record, not the oracle gap. Do not promise more.

source: Select-then-Solve (2026): training size and token cost
finding: Router labels came from about 300 to 400 examples per model (532 train, 229 test, 70/30 stratified). Router cost is small next to paradigm cost. Bears on gap 4 and on equal-token comparison.
numbers: Tokens relative to Direct: CoT 1.0 to 1.1x, ReCode 2.8x, ReAct 4.0x, Plan-Execute 6.9x, Reflection 9.4x. GPT-5 per task: router about 7.0k tokens, always-Direct 3.5k, always-ReAct 14.0k.
limits: No learning curve, so minimum data per class is not measured. No equal-token comparison against the best single paradigm. Authors say a larger set would likely help.
agent_relevance: A router can be cheaper than the strongest fixed operator and better than it. Equal-token tests should include cost-aware routing.

finding: Letting the model pick its own paradigm from a prompt does not beat Direct for most models. Answers gap 8 and part of gap 3: prompt-side choice lost to code-side learned routing on the same items.
numbers: Table 7 self-route vs Direct: GPT-5 60.3 vs 60.3; Gemini 56.8 vs 55.5; Qwen3-Max 42.4 vs 49.8 (worse); Qwen3-30B 27.5 vs 24.9; mean 46.7 vs 47.6. Text says GPT-5 67.1 and mean 48.4, which disagrees with the table. GPT-5 picks Direct 65.1 percent of the time; no model ever picks Reflection.
limits: Self-route prompt gave paradigm descriptions only, no per-class pass rates. It tests self-selection (Self-Discover style), not a written record.
agent_relevance: Self-selection has a strength threshold that even frontier models barely pass. Route in code with measured rates.

source: Cross-check of Select-then-Solve design: self-route vs router is confounded
finding: Self-route and learned router differ in two ways at once: who decides (model vs code) and what information it has (none vs training labels). Gap 3 is therefore not cleanly closed by this paper.
numbers: No arm gives the model the learned class pass rates in the prompt. MIRROR (opened earlier) is the only prompt-vs-code test and it is about confidence.
limits: Inference from the design of Table 7, not a measured result.
agent_relevance: Our own ablation must run record-in-prompt vs record-in-code on the same items.

source: Route to Reason (RTR, 2025) Adaptive Routing for LLM and Reasoning Strategy Selection
finding: Routing jointly over model and strategy (Vanilla, CoT, PAL, CoD) beats the strongest single model and random choice, at under half the tokens.
numbers: In-distribution (GSM8K 600, Math 600, MMLU 600, OlympiadBench 300): RTR 82.5 percent at 1091 tokens; QwQ-32B 80.0 at 2745; EmbedLLM 81.9 at 1808; KNN-Router 76.9; RouteLLM 77.3; Random (50 runs) 69.5 at 1272. Unseen sets (SciQ, PIQA, ARC-C, 300 each): RTR 94.2 vs QwQ 93.7 vs random 79.0; tokens 394 vs 1387.
limits: Beats random by 13 points but the best single model by only 2.5 (ID) and 0.5 (OOD). Single run, no CIs. Text inconsistent on 6 vs 7 models and on training size.
agent_relevance: Supplies the missing random-control (gaps 1, 7): random choice loses about 10 points to the best model, so router value is mostly cost saving.

source: Route to Reason (2025): transfer to unseen tasks and training data
finding: A router trained on four sets transfers to three unseen sets. Supports task-side transfer of a learned record (gap 5 partly).
numbers: Unseen-set accuracy: PIQA 95.3, SciQ 94.2, ARC-C 93.1. Training about 1470 cases (70 percent of 2100; derived, not stated); paper elsewhere says convergence near 5000. Qwen3-4B thinking vs non-thinking routing: 83.8 percent at 1321 tokens vs thinking 82.4 at 3113 vs non-thinking 73.4 at 592.
limits: Unseen sets are easy (all near 94 percent), so ceiling effects hide transfer failure. No mixed-class items. No transfer to another model.
agent_relevance: Transfer to easy new classes is weak evidence for transfer to mixed or hard ones.

source: Semantic Router for vLLM (2025) intent-aware reasoning mode selection
finding: A small fine-tuned classifier decides in code whether to switch reasoning on. Code-side gating raised accuracy and halved tokens on MMLU-Pro.
numbers: Qwen3-30B-A3B, MMLU-Pro, 14 domains: accuracy 58.57 vs 48.33 (+10.24 pp, p<0.01); latency 13.09 s vs 24.76 s (-47.1 percent); tokens 887.5 vs 1722.1 (-48.5 percent). Better in 11 of 14 domains; largest in business and economics (over 20 pp); mixed in math and biology.
limits: Baseline is one direct serving config, not the best fixed mode. No variance or run count. Engineering report, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Supports gap 3: class-conditioned gating outside the model is cheap and works for a binary operator choice; weakest where reasoning is needed.

source: From Knowing to Acting: Benchmarking Self-Awareness Capability of LLM Agents (2026), KAPRO / KAware
finding: Separates knowing whether a task needs a tool from acting on it. Knowing and acting diverge, and differ by model. Relevant to gap 6 and Flavell's 'known but ignored' failure (gap 10).
numbers: 1076 tasks (310 external, 368 hybrid, 398 internal), 18 models, zero-shot greedy. Internal subspace Acc_know vs Acc_act: GPT-5 94.22 vs 58.54; GPT-5.5 68.09 vs 32.66; GPT-4o 24.37 vs 46.48; Qwen3-235B-instruct 8.04 vs 45.48. Kc/Aw (knew no tool needed, used one anyway): GPT-5.5 45.48, Sonnet 4.5 think 41.96, GPT-5 38.94, Qwen3-235B-instruct 1.76 percent. Pearson r = -0.748 (p<0.001) between knowing score and tool calls on internal tasks. Label agreement with humans 90.41 percent.
limits: Only the first 100k characters of the page were read; no numeric success correlation seen. Diagnostic only. Generation and judging by GPT-5 and GPT-4.1.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models often know a tool is not needed yet use it. A written rule must be enforced in code (gaps 3, 10).

source: KAPRO (2026): abstract claim on model type vs table
finding: Abstract: open-source and instruction models overuse tools; proprietary and reasoning models gate more reliably. Table partly disagrees: reasoning variants show higher Kc/Aw.
numbers: Kc/Aw: Sonnet 4.5 think 41.96 vs Sonnet 4.5 instruct 23.12; Qwen3-235B think 19.85 vs instruct 1.76; DeepSeek-V4-flash 27.89.
limits: Direction of the model-type effect is unsettled in the text read.
agent_relevance: Do not use model type as a proxy for good gating. Measure our model.

source: LLMs learn different forms of metacognition when trained to predict their own accuracy (2026)
finding: Training a model to report confidence yields two self-knowledge skills: tracking true accuracy (local) and tracking output consistency (transfers far). Bears on gaps 5 and 6.
numbers: 10 open 3B to 9B models, 4-bit. Verbal confidence r=0.04 before training, r=0.73 after. Qwen3.5-9B on MedMCQA: confidence vs consistency r=0.94, vs accuracy r=0.81; on Math r=0.99 with accuracy. Trained on Math: accuracy tracking on Math (delta r=+0.23), consistency tracking on MMLU-Pro and MedMCQA (delta r=-0.14). Consistency tracking grows with distance from training data (r=0.49).
limits: Factual multiple choice, no chain of thought, small quantized models, few datasets. Before/after use different elicitation formats (confound). Weights are trained; our scaffold cannot.
agent_relevance: A self-knowledge record learned on one class tends to decay into a generic consistency signal on far classes. Expect weak transfer; recheck per class.

source: Bandits in Prod (2026) Hyperparameter Optimization at Inference Time
finding: Online many-armed bandit; active arm set grows as sqrt(t); 10 baseline arms served once before learned proposals. A cold-start recipe and regret bound for choosing configurations online (gap 4).
numbers: Warm-up 10 configurations, each once. Active set |M_t| < t^0.5. Regret O(p rho^(-1/beta) + T^((1+beta)/2)), T^0.75 at beta=0.5. HotpotQA: 5000 online questions then 500 held out, 5 seeds; TabPFN oracle lowest online regret. Delayed-feedback case keeps about 60 arms, about 33 rewards per arm.
limits: No explicit sample count at which a measured rate beats a prior. No token cost. Most rewards are surrogates. A learned oracle sometimes trails a hierarchical bandit.
agent_relevance: Cold start: try every operator on a few items per class first. Drop hand priors only after tens of observations per arm (our count still unmeasured).

source: PRISM (2025) Plan before Solving: Problem-Aware Strategy Routing for Mathematical Reasoning
finding: A small adapter picks among math strategies from the problem. Gain over the best fixed strategy is real but modest; the paper's own numbers conflict.
numbers: Pass@1 mean over 5 math sets: Qwen2.5-Math-7B CoT 61.0, PAL 46.6, ToRA 61.9, PRISM 70.7; DeepSeek-Math-7B CoT 68.6, PRISM 72.4; Llama-3-8B best single 33.4, PRISM 42.5. Training about 13,000 instances. Stated gains 0.9, 2.9, 7.6 percent do not match the table (+8.8, +3.8, +9.1 vs best single).
limits: No oracle, no router accuracy, no limitations section. Method and baseline strategy names do not map. 13k labels is far above what a scaffold record would have.
agent_relevance: Routing helps most where strategies differ a lot (PAL vs CoT differ 15 points on Qwen) and little where the top ones are close.

source: Vadlapati (2025) Reasoning Router: Dynamic Multi-Strategy Reasoning for Robust Multi-Step Problem Solving
finding: Single-author preprint claiming 6 to 12 point gains over single-strategy baselines. Seen only as a search summary.
limits: Not opened. Do not use for claims.
agent_relevance: Listed so it is not rediscovered later.

source: Implementation of a Metacognition Framework for Self-Awareness and Self-Regulation in Ensembles of LLMs (2026)
finding: Metacognitive State Vector with five dimensions, gated by fixed thresholds in code (System 1 vs 2, early stop at 85 percent confidence or conflict below 20 percent). No benchmarks.
numbers: Llama 3.2 on a laptop, three illustrative queries, no quantitative result, thresholds hand-set.
limits: Self-reported scores with no validation. A design sketch, not evidence.
agent_relevance: Same shape as our code-side gating; no evidence for or against.

source: Gap 10 cross-check: Flavell failure rates under a written class record
finding: No opened study reports the rate of the four Flavell failures (wrong, not retrieved, ignored, unhelpful) when a written class record is used. Closest proxies: KAPRO Kc/Aw and Select-then-Solve self-route.
numbers: KAPRO Kc/Aw range 1.76 to 45.48 percent over 18 models (internal tasks). Self-route: GPT-5 picks Direct 65.1 percent; none picks Reflection.
limits: Proxies only; neither study supplied a record.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open; log the four failure types in our own runs.
